items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Little Ray Romero. We recorded that in a place called Incredible Sounds, for Morris Levy.

ctx.x: Then let’s do that. Let’s talk about Justicia.

In Justicia we talk about the injustice to the Indian, to the blacks, to everyone down the line, and with my call to the drum, “....(?—28:27).... del tambor,” “I recall justice.” And then I met a gentleman in Venezuela. His name was Francisco Luna, a newspaperman. I tell him, “The son or daughter of justice, who would it be? La Libertad or (?—28;44)?” That’s when I did “La Libertad” also. On Justicia is Francisco Aguabella playing conga; Chino Pozo, the great bongo player that worked with Tito Puente; and…
